title: Orthogonal Functions
body:
Two functions $f$ and $g$ are orthogonal  $\iff \int_{a}^b f(x)g(x)dx = 0$

This is the [[Dot Product]] condition $\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0$ with the sum replaced by
an integral. Functions on $[a,b]$ form a [[Vector Space]], an orthogonal family is a [[Basis]]
for it, and a [[Fourier Coefficients|Fourier coefficient]] is the projection onto one basis
element. See [[LINEAR ALGEBRA]].

An [[Orthonormal Basis]] in [[LINEAR ALGEBRA FOR DATA SCIENCE]] (MATH 2303) is the
finite-dimensional case of the same statement: this course does it with an integral and infinitely
many basis elements, that one does it with a sum and $n$ of them. The
[[Projection]] formula, coefficient by coefficient, is identical in both.
